clue.text: Consider more passable, say, for traveller

indicators.note: say tells us the phrase before it is to be spoken, and the entry is what it sounds like

parts.note: to consider is to weigh, and more passable is fairer: weigh fairer

explanation.surface: Someone judging which route is easier, framed as a riddle about a traveller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks a sound-alike: WEIGH FAIRER, spoken, gives the entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A wayfarer is a synonym for someone journeying, especially on foot.

clue.text: Pals teed off in base

indicators.note: off suggests the letters have gone wrong or awry, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Golfing friends who have teed off from the base of the course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' looks like part of the golf phrase 'teed off' but signals the rearrangement of PALS TEED.
explanation.definitionFit: A plinth or base on which a statue stands is a synonym for this support.

clue.text: Bonus for each is accepted by all

parts.note: per means for each, as in 'per head'

indicators.note: accepted by means taken inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: quite can mean entirely or all, as in 'quite finished'

explanation.surface: A bonus paid to every worker, which everyone accepts happily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all' here is the adverb meaning completely, as in 'quite done'.
explanation.definitionFit: A perk or fringe benefit is a bonus on top of a salary.

clue.text: Father's breaking fast in pope's office

indicators.note: breaking means splitting another word open by getting inside it

parts.note: pacy means quick or fast
pa is father, with 's read as 'is'

explanation.surface: A priest breaking a fast during his time in the papal office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Father's' reads as 'Father is', and 'fast' means quick, not abstaining from food.
explanation.definitionFit: The papacy is the position or tenure of the head of the Roman Catholic Church.

clue.text: Genuine old coin, Spanish

definitions.meaning: a former silver coin of Spain

explanation.surface: A collector's note authenticating a Spanish coin as genuine.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means authentic, and was also the name of an old Spanish silver coin.

clue.text: What may have been held up if 'Rain stopped play'?

definitions.text: What may have been held up if 'Rain stopped play'?

parts.words: What may have been held up if 'Rain stopped play'?
parts.note: held up reads as delayed, like a match, but here means raised over a spectator's head in the shower

explanation.surface: Cricket scoreboard announcement: play was halted for rain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held up' suggests a delayed match; really it is the rain shield lifted overhead. 'Rain stopped play' is the classic British cricket notice.
explanation.definitionFit: Raised over one's head, this canopy device stops rain reaching the holder.

clue.text: Cast off, beginning to sail on Irish lake

indicators.note: beginning to points to the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: lough is the Irish word for a lake

explanation.surface: A boat casting off and setting sail on an Irish lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast off' sounds nautical but is the verb for shedding skin, as a snake does.
explanation.definitionFit: To slough is to shed or discard, as a snake drops its old skin.

clue.text: Article close to my doodah

parts.note: an article is an object or thing

indicators.note: close to means the end letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: An item lying near some gadget whose name escapes the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' suggests A or THE, but here it is an object.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal placeholder words for an object whose name one cannot recall.

clue.text: Arrived ahead of artist, producer of pictures

parts.note: came means arrived
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter turned up before the film-maker.
explanation.definitionFit: This device takes photographs, so it produces pictures.

clue.text: Delicious food in bar? I am so mistaken

indicators.note: mistaken means wrong, so these letters are wrongly ordered and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone in a pub doubting they are right about the tasty food on offer.
explanation.definitionFit: In myth this was the food of the gods, so anything deliciously tasty.

clue.text: Following each one in spite of everything

parts.note: after means following
all means every one, each one

explanation.surface: Someone persists, following everyone, regardless.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means nevertheless or despite all that happened.

clue.text: Meet in battle and swear to marry?

definitions.meaning: to fight an enemy, joining combat
to bind by promise to wed, as with a ring

explanation.surface: A wry take on a quarrelsome couple whose courtship is also a war.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to join combat with and to pledge to wed, as in 'become engaged'.

clue.text: More or less charming mineral spring

parts.note: pretty means charming or attractive
a well is a spring of water, as in a spa town's wells

explanation.surface: A spa spring that is, roughly speaking, quite attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means almost or nearly, as in 'I'd nearly finished'.

clue.text: Best English, low in calories

parts.note: lite is the marketing spelling for a low-calorie product

explanation.surface: A diet label boasting the best English low-calorie food.
explanation.definitionFit: The best of a group, its top members, form the cream or chosen few.

clue.text: Patriotic song, Arne air Butlin's broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are spread and reformed

parts.note: the possessive 's gives no letter

explanation.surface: A patriotic tune by Arne played over the speakers at a Butlin's holiday camp.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Arne composed this song; Butlin's is a chain of British holiday camps. Rearrange ARNE AIR BUTLIN.
explanation.definitionFit: This rousing 1740 tune about Britain's naval supremacy is a classic patriotic anthem.

clue.text: Astound boyfriend, said partner in affair

indicators.note: said marks the preceding word as spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: a beau is a boyfriend
a lover is a partner in a love affair

explanation.surface: Someone stunning their boyfriend, said to be having an affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' applies only to the boyfriend: BEAU sounds like BOW.
explanation.definitionFit: To astound is to amaze someone so much that they are figuratively knocked flat.

clue.text: In tune, possibly, about right time to give a nourishing substance

indicators.note: about means going round, so these letters enclose another
possibly signals the letters may be arranged in another way

explanation.surface: A singer told to stay in tune at the right moment to give out good things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' turns IN TUNE into NUTIEN, and 'about' wraps it round R; T follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Any substance that feeds the body, such as a vitamin or protein, is one.

clue.text: Olympic Games host accommodating a fast runner

indicators.note: accommodating means housing within, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: Atlanta, Georgia, hosted the 1996 Olympics

explanation.surface: An Olympic host city housing a sprinter.
explanation.walkthrough: The runner is the swift huntress of Greek myth, not an athlete at the Games.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this huntress was famously swift, racing her suitors.

clue.text: In US wedding centre, Irish artist

parts.note: Reno, Nevada is known for quick weddings and divorces

explanation.surface: An Irish painter getting married in Nevada.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierre-Auguste of this name was a French Impressionist painter.

clue.text: Everything eaten by female elephant is green

indicators.note: eaten by means swallowed inside another word

parts.note: a female elephant is called a cow
all means everything

explanation.surface: A cow elephant chewing everything in sight, all of it green vegetation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green' looks like a colour but means inexperienced.
explanation.definitionFit: Green in the sense of naive or inexperienced, like an untested youth.

clue.text: Wife with male, more attractive in retirement, in the fashionable place to be

parts.note: he is the male pronoun

indicators.note: in retirement means drawing back, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: tastier can mean more attractive

explanation.surface: A retired couple find themselves at the trendiest spot in town.
explanation.definitionFit: This idiom names the hub of fashionable activity, where the trendy crowd goes.

clue.text: Go by the Spanish church recess

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
an apse is a vaulted recess at a church's end

explanation.surface: Instructions to pass a Spanish church's alcove.
explanation.definitionFit: When time passes, we say it lapses away or goes by.

clue.text: Told stories recalled about volunteers, soldiers given a special task

indicators.note: about means surrounding the following piece
recalled suggests calling back, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: lied means told stories, told fibs
TA is the Territorial Army, the British reserve of volunteer soldiers

explanation.surface: Volunteer soldiers telling tales about their mission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' gives DEIL, read backwards; 'about' wraps it round the volunteers.
explanation.definitionFit: A military squad assigned to a particular duty is called this, e.g. a guard party.

clue.text: Weight of importance? No end, since eating Italian

indicators.note: eating means taking another piece inside
no end means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: grave means serious, of importance
as can mean since or because
IT is short for Italian, as in vermouth

explanation.surface: A dieter asks whether weight matters endlessly while eating Italian food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weight of importance?' looks like one phrase, but only 'Weight' defines; 'No end' trims the synonym for 'of importance'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gravitas means seriousness or dignity, the weight a person carries.

clue.text: Good boy, eager

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: Praise for a keen youngster.
explanation.definitionFit: Glad as in 'glad to help' means willing or eager.

clue.text: Where's the penthouse suite of the highest office?

definitions.meaning: the luxury flat is located on the uppermost floor of the building
involving those of most senior rank, as in summit talks

explanation.surface: A question about where the executive suite of the chief officer lies.
explanation.definitionFit: The penthouse is on the uppermost storey, and the adjective means involving the most senior people.

clue.text: Musical composition person at auditorium includes

indicators.note: includes means the letters are held within the words before it

explanation.surface: A concert-goer in the hall containing a piece of music.
explanation.definitionFit: A work for one or a few instruments, usually in several movements.

clue.text: This may help protect castle in game following stalemate

indicators.note: following means the game piece comes after the stalemate piece

parts.note: a stalemate is a draw, a game with no winner
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: Chess talk: a stalemate in which the castle is protected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'castle' and 'stalemate' suggest chess; the castle is a real fortress.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinged bridge over a moat that can be raised to keep attackers out.
